subject: module:agents
claim: 26 single-purpose reference agents, one directory per agent, each a separate npm package with its own `bin`. 25 of the 26 import `sdk/typescript` for the protocol envelope (the exception is `agents/llm` itself, which the other 9 LLM-backed agents import for the tool loop: coder, planner, reviewer, pr-opener, issue-opener, issue-triage, policy-check, notion-worker, runtime); the rest are mechanical adapters over one vendor API. Each agent observes or acts on ONE task and emits protocol events — routing, retries, loop limits, durable state and webhooks are deliberately the orchestrator's, outside this repo. That boundary is why a per-agent claim says almost nothing: the interesting structure is the fleet, not the members.

subject: module:agents/llm
claim: agents/llm is a shared LLM-runtime package (`@anchorage/agent-llm`) whose index.ts is a single re-export surface for the tool loop, provider adapters (Anthropic, Bedrock, OpenAI), the builtin tool catalogs (repo, shell, web, notion, symbols, discovery), and the loop's public types, so consumer agents avoid deep imports.

subject: module:agents/llm
claim: The module owns provider selection/configuration by env var: `ANCHORAGE_LLM_PROVIDER` selects one of anthropic | aws-bedrock | openai, and named OpenAI-compatible presets (e.g. openrouter) map a preset name to a base URL, credential env var, and default model, with raw `openai` + `OPENAI_BASE_URL` as the escape hatch.

subject: module:agents/llm
claim: Model defaults are centralized per agent role in ROLE_DEFAULTS, which gives each role (planner, coder, reviewer, triage, runtime, notion-worker, issue-opener, pr-opener) an anthropic/bedrock/openai model triple; agents pass their row to `resolveLlmConfig` and per-deploy overrides come from `ANCHORAGE_LLM_MODEL` / `ANCHORAGE_<ROLE>_MODEL`.

subject: module:agents/llm
claim: The tool loop enforces capability-gated tool exposure and a sandboxed workspace: `runWithTools` takes a workspacePath plus a capabilities list, filters the tool catalog so tools whose capability wasn't granted (e.g. write_file under workspace.write) never reach the provider, emits tool.requested/tool.result events, and returns a snapshot of tool turns and files read.

subject: module:agents/llm
claim: policy.ts implements pure, storage-agnostic architecture governance: it parses `.anchorage/constraints.yaml` with a dependency-free tolerant parser (degrading to zero rules plus warnings on failure) and evaluates `forbid-import` rules against an injected ImportGraphView, with hard violations intended to trigger a code.revision.request between apply-code and run-tests.

subject: module:agents/llm
claim: prompts.ts centralizes cross-agent system-prompt rules so wording cannot drift between coder/planner/reviewer/triage: GRAPH_FIRST_RULE mandates using index tools (repo_map, locate_change, impact, find_references) instead of grep for named symbols, and BATCH_TOOL_CALLS_RULE tells agents to issue 3-8 independent tool calls per reply to avoid per-turn round-trip cost.

subject: module:sdk/typescript
claim: sdk/typescript is a shared protocol/contract library whose single entry point re-exports artifact builders, CI conclusion classification, event-stream parsing/validation, exit codes, run manifests, JSON schemas, and validators for downstream agents and the orchestrator.

subject: module:sdk/typescript
claim: Schema validation is JSON-Schema based: the module imports four protocol schema JSON documents from the external @anchorage/protocol package and exposes typed validators keyed by canonical https://anchorage.dev/schemas/... $ids for artifact references, agent manifests, protocol events, and task envelopes.

subject: module:sdk/typescript
claim: The module owns canonical artifact type constants and normalizing builders that define the agent-to-orchestrator contract — e.g. `code.revision.request` (tester→coder feedback loop) and `runtime.preview` (runtime agent→orchestrator pre-merge approval gate) — including bounding failure detail excerpts to 4000 characters so artifacts travelling in the task envelope cannot balloon.

subject: module:sdk/typescript
claim: CI check-run conclusion semantics are centralized here as one vocabulary shared by the ci-watcher and merge-gate agents, using explicit blocking/passing allowlists and a fail-closed default so an unrecognised GitHub conclusion blocks a merge rather than passing silently.

subject: module:agents/runtime
claim: agents/runtime is a standalone CLI agent that reads a TaskEnvelope from stdin, only accepts tasks of type `runtime.start`, and requires `input.workspacePath` to point at an existing repository worktree directory — emitting protocol events and typed exit codes (UnsupportedTaskType, InvalidInput) otherwise.

subject: module:agents/runtime
claim: It owns a pure, I/O-free change classifier that gates the visual preview: docs files are stripped first, any backend/non-UI path signal (api/server/db/migrations dirs, route.ts, .sql/.py/.go, etc.) wins over visual signals, and non-matching changes fall to 'non-visual' — each non-visual kind mapping to a human-readable skip reason so the gate is skipped rather than failing the PR.

subject: module:agents/runtime
claim: The preview strategy is deliberately isolation-based rather than booting the app: a throwaway Vite harness is written under `<appRoot>/.anchorage/preview/` that imports only the changed components via generated stories and never the app entry point, so it runs without the app's auth/DB/secret dependencies; app fidelity is preserved by reusing the app's PostCSS config, tsconfig path aliases, and a de-duped framework runtime copy.

subject: module:agents/runtime
claim: It implements a two-tier harness generation pipeline: deterministic per-framework templates in a FRAMEWORK_TEMPLATES registry (React/Preact, Vue, Svelte, Solid) with fallback to an agentic LLM path (`@anchorage/agent-llm` tool loop with repo read/write and shell tools) that terminates via a single `submit_preview` tool returning framework, installCommand and startCommand; index.ts remains the deterministic driver that installs, starts detached and probes, feeding startup errors back for one repair pass.

subject: module:agents/runtime
claim: The agent caches its discovered run recipe on disk under a repo-local `.anchorage/` directory — `runtime.json` for the run strategy and `preview.json` for the working harness (framework, generator template|llm, install/start commands, port) — with parsing/serialization kept pure and strictly validated so malformed caches return null and force rediscovery.

subject: module:agents/runtime
claim: Readiness is budgeted per run strategy with an explicit polling loop — docker-compose gets 180s (image builds), node 90s, static 20s, polled every 1s, with a separately configurable install timeout via ANCHORAGE_RUNTIME_INSTALL_TIMEOUT_MS.

subject: module:agents/runtime
claim: The harness exposes a dedicated server-side render probe route `/__anchorage/render` so the orchestrator can distinguish components that actually render from those that throw for missing context/props, which a plain HTTP GET of the client-rendered SPA shell cannot detect; those render failures are then fed into the LLM path as `renderFailures` so it can wrap the offending components in mocked providers.

subject: module:agents/coder
claim: agents/coder is a standalone CLI agent that reads a task envelope from stdin, accepts only `code.change` tasks (exiting with `ExitCode.UnsupportedTaskType` otherwise), and emits protocol lifecycle events such as `agent.started`, `agent.progress` and `agent.failed`.

subject: module:agents/coder
claim: It drives an LLM tool loop supplied by the shared `@anchorage/agent-llm` package — importing `runWithTools` plus discovery, repo read/write, shell and web tool sets and LLM config resolution — and depends on `@anchorage/sdk` for envelope validation and protocol types, so the agent owns orchestration rather than model plumbing.

subject: module:agents/coder
claim: The module owns git branch lifecycle for a coding run: `branch.ts` scopes a planner-proposed branch name with a 12-character git-safe TAIL of the run id (idempotently, falling back to `fix/changes`) so concurrent runs on the same issue cannot collide, and lets a previous `code.change` artifact's branch win so a revision cycle adds commits to the existing PR.

subject: module:agents/coder
claim: index.ts resolves the working branch defensively against the remote: a revision request only preserves the existing branch when `remoteBranchExists` confirms it, and a `reuseBranch` from a run being corrected is adopted only if it still exists, otherwise the run warns and falls back to the plan's run-scoped branch (fresh PR).

subject: module:agents/coder
claim: `summary.ts` is the tolerant parser for the model's final report: it uses `parseModelJsonObject` from `@anchorage/sdk` to find JSON inside prose/fences, drops non-string entries, and degrades to the first 800 characters of raw text rather than reporting silence — behaviour pinned by dependency-free node:test suites that run against the built `dist`.

subject: module:agents/bitbucket-pr-opener
claim: This module is a standalone CLI agent that reads a task envelope from stdin, accepts only the `bitbucket.pull_request.open` task type, and exits with SDK-defined exit codes (UnsupportedTaskType, MissingCapability, ExternalDependencyFailure) for each failure mode.

subject: module:agents/bitbucket-pr-opener
claim: The agent depends on `@anchorage/sdk` for its shared contract — task envelope types/validation, protocol events, exit codes, and the `resolveOrCreatePr` idempotency helper — so PR creation is deduplicated by looking up an existing open PR for the branch before creating a new one, avoiding duplicate PRs on retried or resumed runs.

subject: module:agents/bitbucket-pr-opener
claim: The agent narrates its work as a stream of protocol events (`agent.started`, `tool.requested`, `tool.result`, `agent.failed`) tagged with tool names like `bitbucket.pullrequests.create` and `bitbucket.pullrequests.list`, rather than returning a plain result.

subject: module:agents/bitbucket-pr-opener
claim: PR title/description rendering is deliberately factored out of `index.ts` into a pure, network-free `pr.ts` module so it can be unit tested; `buildTitle` falls back from the summary's first line (capped at 72 chars) to `Resolve issue #N` to a de-slugged branch name, and `buildDescription` guarantees non-empty Summary and Changed files sections.

subject: module:agents/bitbucket-pr-opener
claim: The agent is one member of a family of per-forge PR openers (`gitlab-pr-opener`, GitHub `pr-opener`) that share this rendering logic, differing only in the attribution line and, for GitHub, section set and a 60-character title ceiling.

subject: module:agents/bitbucket-pr-opener
claim: Authentication and endpoint are environment-driven: `BITBUCKET_TOKEN` is required (used as the `x-token-auth` credential when pushing the branch) and `BITBUCKET_API_BASE_URL` overrides the default `https://api.bitbucket.org` host.

subject: module:agents/bitbucket-reader
claim: bitbucket-reader is a stdin-driven CLI agent that reads a TaskEnvelope from fd 0, accepts only the `bitbucket.task.read` task type, and returns structured ExitCode values (UnsupportedTaskType, InvalidInput, MissingCapability, ExternalDependencyFailure, Success) from the shared @anchorage/sdk contract.

subject: module:agents/bitbucket-reader
claim: The agent communicates progress via a protocol event stream, emitting a fixed lifecycle sequence of agent.started, tool.requested/tool.result, agent.output, artifact.created, and agent.completed or agent.failed events with severity and structured payloads.

subject: module:agents/bitbucket-reader
claim: Issue-reference parsing is the module's own extracted abstraction (`parseIssueRef` in ref.ts) that maps a human-written string plus an optional repository hint to a `{repo, id}` identifier, deliberately returning null rather than guessing; it was split out of index.ts so the accepted forms can be tested without a token or network.

subject: module:agents/bitbucket-reader
claim: The agent normalizes Bitbucket's issue model into a repo-agnostic IssueSummary: it collapses resolved/closed/invalid/duplicate/wontfix states to "closed" (everything else "open"), and — because Bitbucket issues have no labels — synthesizes labels from the issue's kind and priority fields.

subject: module:agents/bitbucket-reader
claim: Bitbucket access is configured purely through environment variables: BITBUCKET_TOKEN (an OAuth access token, required or the run fails with MissingCapability) and an overridable BITBUCKET_API_BASE_URL defaulting to https://api.bitbucket.org, with issues fetched from the /2.0/repositories/{repo}/issues/{id} REST endpoint.

subject: module:agents/bitbucket-reader
claim: Tests are dependency-free node:test suites that exercise the compiled output (../dist/ref.js) rather than the TypeScript source, pinning the accepted reference forms including the regression where `#42` was rejected while `42` worked.

subject: module:agents/ci-watcher
claim: ci-watcher is a standalone CLI agent that reads a JSON TaskEnvelope from stdin, accepts only tasks of type `ci.watch`, and terminates with SDK-defined exit codes (Success, InvalidInput, MissingCapability, Timeout, PartialSuccessAttentionRequired) depending on the CI outcome.

subject: module:agents/ci-watcher
claim: It polls GitHub via Octokit for a pull request's combined check runs and commit statuses, using a configurable poll interval and max poll count, and requires a GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_TOKEN or it fails with a `missing_github_token` capability error.

subject: module:agents/ci-watcher
claim: The agent reports progress as a stream of protocol events (agent.started, tool.requested, tool.result, agent.output, artifact.created, agent.completed/agent.failed) and persists the CI report as an artifact on disk before exiting.

subject: module:agents/ci-watcher
claim: Verdict phrasing is isolated in `summarize.ts`, a pure function mapping (status, failed checks, pending checks) to one human-readable line that must name the specific failing/pending checks and falls back to "unknown check"/"checks not complete" rather than an empty list.

subject: module:agents/ci-watcher
claim: It depends on `@anchorage/sdk` for shared cross-agent vocabulary — envelope validation plus conclusion/status predicates (checkConclusionBlocks, checkRunIsPending, commitStatusBlocks) that are deliberately shared with the merge-gate agent so both agree on what a blocking conclusion is.

subject: module:agents/deploy-watch
claim: deploy-watch is a stdin-driven CLI agent that reads a JSON TaskEnvelope from fd 0, validates it with @anchorage/sdk's validateTaskEnvelope, and rejects any task whose type is not 'deploy.watch' with ExitCode.UnsupportedTaskType.

subject: module:agents/deploy-watch
claim: The agent communicates progress through a sequence of protocol events (agent.started, agent.output, artifact.created, agent.failed/agent.completed) and maps outcomes onto SDK exit codes: InvalidInput for unparseable/invalid task, PartialSuccessAttentionRequired when the deployment status is not a recognised success, Success otherwise.

subject: module:agents/deploy-watch
claim: Its concrete side effect is writing a 'deployment.record' JSON artifact (deployment-record.json) to ANCHORAGE_ARTIFACT_DIR or a per-run temp directory keyed by task.run.id, and reporting the file:// URI, media type and byte size back in an artifact.created event.

subject: module:agents/deploy-watch
claim: Success detection is owned by status.ts as a deliberate case-insensitive exact-match allowlist of exactly four statuses ('deployed','ready','succeeded','success'); unrecognised, empty, or near-miss statuses (e.g. 'successful', 'successfully deployed') are treated as not-deployed.

subject: module:agents/deploy-watch
claim: Deployment input parsing is lenient: missing id/environment/status fields default to 'deployment_local'/'unknown'/'unknown' rather than failing, so an absent status flows into the allowlist check and yields a non-success verdict instead of an error.

subject: module:agents/deployer
claim: The deployer is a stdin-driven CLI agent that reads a TaskEnvelope from fd 0, accepts only tasks of type `deploy.trigger` (emitting `agent.failed` with `unsupported_task_type` and ExitCode.UnsupportedTaskType otherwise), and emits protocol lifecycle events such as `agent.started` and `tool.requested`.

subject: module:agents/deployer
claim: Deployment goes through GitHub via Octokit authenticated from GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_TOKEN; a missing token is a hard failure (ExitCode.MissingCapability), and the agent first tries to auto-detect a workflow_dispatch deploy workflow, falling back to the GitHub Deployments API.

subject: module:agents/deployer
claim: Missing preconditions (no environment selected, no GitHub repo on the task, no branch to deploy) are treated as non-blocking 'not applicable' outcomes rather than failures, so the pipeline continues to PR; the branch defaults to the workspace's checked-out git branch via `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`.

subject: module:agents/deployer
claim: `detect.ts` owns only the ORDERING of candidate workflow files — a token-based filename score (deploy=3, whole-token `cd`/release/stage/ship=2, otherwise 0) plus a name tie-break for determinism — while eligibility (workflow_dispatch + environment input) is decided elsewhere by reading each file.

subject: module:agents/deployer
claim: The agent bounds how long it blocks on the deploy becoming live: it polls every 6s up to a watch timeout (default 240s, floor 30s, overridable by ANCHORAGE_DEPLOY_WATCH_TIMEOUT_MS) and then stops blocking while the GitHub deploy continues.

subject: module:agents/deployer
claim: It shares the cross-agent contract from `@anchorage/sdk`, importing envelope validation and deploy-preview artifact builders/types (buildDeployPreview, DEPLOY_PREVIEW_ARTIFACT_TYPE, DeployTrigger, ProtocolEvent), indicating its output is a deploy-preview artifact consumed downstream.

subject: module:agents/gitlab-pr-opener
claim: gitlab-pr-opener is a standalone CLI agent that reads a task envelope from stdin, accepts only tasks of type `gitlab.merge_request.open`, and exits with typed SDK exit codes (UnsupportedTaskType, MissingCapability, ExternalDependencyFailure) for each failure mode.

subject: module:agents/gitlab-pr-opener
claim: The agent pushes the change branch and creates the merge request via the GitLab API using a GITLAB_TOKEN (oauth2 user) against a configurable GITLAB_BASE_URL that defaults to https://gitlab.com.

subject: module:agents/gitlab-pr-opener
claim: Idempotency of MR creation is delegated to the shared `resolveOrCreatePr` helper from @anchorage/sdk: a pre-check lists open MRs for the source branch so retried/resumed runs reuse the prior MR, and the pre-check fails open (emitting a warn tool.result) rather than aborting.

subject: module:agents/gitlab-pr-opener
claim: The module reports progress as a stream of structured protocol events (agent.started, agent.failed, tool.requested, tool.result) carrying tool names, inputs, success flags and error codes, which is how the rest of the system observes the agent's work.

subject: module:agents/gitlab-pr-opener
claim: PR body rendering is factored into a side-effect-free `pr.ts` module (buildTitle/buildDescription) so it can be unit-tested without a token or network; the title falls back summary-line → issue number → de-slugged branch under a 72-character ceiling, and both description sections always render placeholder content when empty.

subject: module:agents/gitlab-pr-opener
claim: This agent is one of a family of forge-specific PR openers (bitbucket-pr-opener, GitHub pr-opener) that intentionally share the same rendering logic, differing only in the attribution line and title length limit.

subject: module:agents/gitlab-reader
claim: gitlab-reader is a standalone CLI agent that reads a TaskEnvelope from stdin, accepts only the `gitlab.task.read` task type, and returns SDK ExitCode values (UnsupportedTaskType, InvalidInput, MissingCapability, ExternalDependencyFailure, Success) as its process exit status.

subject: module:agents/gitlab-reader
claim: It communicates progress via a structured protocol event stream from @anchorage/sdk — emitting agent.started, tool.requested/tool.result, agent.output, artifact.created, agent.completed and agent.failed events — rather than plain logging.

subject: module:agents/gitlab-reader
claim: The agent fetches a single issue through the GitLab REST v4 API (`/api/v4/projects/{id}/issues/{iid}`), requiring a GITLAB_TOKEN env var (missing token => MissingCapability) and honoring GITLAB_BASE_URL with a default of https://gitlab.com.

subject: module:agents/gitlab-reader
claim: `parseIssueRef` in ref.ts is the module's own reference-resolution abstraction: it accepts GitLab issue URLs, `owner/name#iid`, and bare/`#`-prefixed numbers resolved against the envelope's repository, and returns null instead of guessing when no project can be determined.

subject: module:agents/gitlab-reader
claim: The parser was deliberately extracted from index.ts so its accepted forms can be tested with node:test against the built dist without a token or network access.

subject: module:agents/gitlab-reader
claim: A successful read produces both an agent.output event and a persisted summary artifact describing the issue (number, title, repository, state, labels, body), normalizing missing fields to defaults such as "(untitled)" and an 'open'/'closed' state.

subject: module:agents/issue-closer
claim: issue-closer is a standalone CLI agent that reads a task envelope from stdin, accepts only tasks of type `issue.close`, and rejects anything else with an `unsupported_task_type` failure event and the SDK's UnsupportedTaskType exit code.

subject: module:agents/issue-closer
claim: It performs its work through the GitHub REST API via Octokit — posting a summary comment (`github.issues.createComment`) then setting the issue state to `closed` (`github.issues.update`) — and requires a GITHUB_TOKEN or GH_TOKEN, exiting with MissingCapability when absent.

subject: module:agents/issue-closer
claim: The agent communicates with the rest of the system through the @anchorage/sdk protocol event stream, emitting a lifecycle of `agent.started`, `tool.requested`/`tool.result` around each GitHub call, `agent.output`, and artifact events, and mapping GitHub API errors to ExitCode.ExternalDependencyFailure.

subject: module:agents/issue-closer
claim: Comment rendering is a separately owned, pure abstraction (`IssueCloseComment` + `buildComment`/`formatValue` in comment.ts) extracted from index.ts so it can be unit-tested without Octokit; it renders a fixed 'Anchorage Run Summary' heading, conditional Links/Artifacts sections that drop empty values and omit empty sections, and an attribution footer.

subject: module:agents/issue-closer
claim: The module's tests are dependency-free (node:test + node:assert) and run against the compiled output in ../dist, implying a TypeScript build step precedes testing.

subject: module:agents/issue-opener
claim: issue-opener is a stdin-driven CLI agent that handles only `issue.open` task envelopes: it reads a task envelope from fd 0, rejects other task types with ExitCode.UnsupportedTaskType, and requires GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN before proceeding.

subject: module:agents/issue-opener
claim: The agent's pipeline is: LLM-assisted repository exploration to draft the issue, creation of the real GitHub issue via Octokit's issues.create, then emission of two artifacts — `issue.opened` (a record) and `issue.summary` (consumed downstream by the planner).

subject: module:agents/issue-opener
claim: draft.ts owns the IssueDraft abstraction with two paths: `parseIssueDraft` returns null unless the model reply yields a non-empty trimmed title AND body (filtering labels to non-empty strings), and `fallbackDraft` builds a mechanical issue that states exploration did not complete and embeds the user's instruction verbatim.

subject: module:agents/issue-opener
claim: The module delegates shared concerns to workspace packages rather than reimplementing them: LLM tooling/config and tool-loop execution come from @anchorage/agent-llm, while envelope validation, exit codes, protocol events, and the tolerant model-JSON scan (parseModelJsonObject) come from @anchorage/sdk — the latter explicitly replacing a locally duplicated greedy JSON parser.

subject: module:agents/issue-opener
claim: Behavior is pinned by a dependency-free node:test suite that runs against the built dist output and asserts the drafting invariants (tolerance of prose/fences around JSON, refusal of blank fields, label filtering, verbatim instruction retention, and title truncation at MAX_FALLBACK_TITLE).

subject: module:agents/issue-reader
claim: issue-reader is a standalone CLI agent that reads a TaskEnvelope as JSON from stdin, validates it with @anchorage/sdk's validateTaskEnvelope, and refuses any task whose type is not `issue.read` with the UnsupportedTaskType exit code.

subject: module:agents/issue-reader
claim: The agent communicates with the orchestrator by emitting a fixed sequence of protocol events (agent.started, tool.requested, agent.output, artifact.created, agent.completed / agent.failed) and returning SDK ExitCode values, mapping failures to codes like InvalidInput and MissingCapability.

subject: module:agents/issue-reader
claim: It fetches the issue from the real GitHub REST API via Octokit, requiring both a repository on the envelope and a GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_TOKEN environment variable, plus a positive integer input.issueNumber.

subject: module:agents/issue-reader
claim: The module owns the `issue.summary` artifact contract: summary.ts totally normalises GitHub's payload (mixed string/object labels filtered to non-empty strings, null body coerced to "", author left nullable) and index.ts persists it as issue-summary.json under ANCHORAGE_ARTIFACT_DIR (or a tmpdir keyed by run id), reporting a file:// URI, media type and size.

subject: module:agents/issue-reader
claim: The summary mapping is deliberately independent of the issue's own URL — the artifact's `repository` field comes from the run's repository argument, so a transferred issue still reports where the work happens — and this is pinned by node:test tests that run against the built dist.

subject: module:agents/issue-triage
claim: issue-triage is a stdin-driven CLI agent: it reads a task envelope from fd 0, rejects any task whose type is not `issue.triage` with ExitCode.UnsupportedTaskType, and reports progress by emitting protocol events (agent.started, tool.requested, tool.result, agent.failed).

subject: module:agents/issue-triage
claim: The agent delegates the triage decision to an LLM tool loop from @anchorage/agent-llm: it resolves the role config via ROLE_DEFAULTS.triage, assembles a tool set (discovery + repo-read tools only when a workspace path exists, plus web tools and a `submit_triage` tool), and calls runWithTools with `submit_triage` as the terminal tool at temperature 0.1.

subject: module:agents/issue-triage
claim: Failure modes map to distinct SDK exit codes: missing LLM credentials or an unsupported provider return ExitCode.MissingCapability, while a failed LLM run returns ExitCode.ExternalDependencyFailure.

subject: module:agents/issue-triage
claim: comment.ts owns pure rendering of the GitHub triage comment, deliberately split from index.ts so tests can import it without the stdin-driven main; it stamps a per-issue marker `<!-- anchorage:triage -->` so retries and re-runs converge on a single comment, and selects one body branch in priority order duplicate > needs-detail questions > agent-eligible > ineligible.

subject: module:agents/issue-triage
claim: The agent runs the LLM loop with ANCHORAGE_GRAPH_FIRST_GUARD=1 so bare-symbol greps are redirected to the code index, an intentional 'graph-first' policy documented inline for repo exploration during issue sizing.

subject: module:agents/jira-reader
claim: jira-reader is a stdin-driven CLI agent that reads a TaskEnvelope from fd 0, accepts only the `jira.task.read` task type, and communicates results by emitting a sequence of protocol events (agent.started, tool.requested/tool.result, agent.output, artifact.created, agent.completed/agent.failed) while signalling outcome through SDK ExitCode values.

subject: module:agents/jira-reader
claim: It fetches issue data from Atlassian Cloud REST API v3 using a JIRA_TOKEN OAuth (3LO) access token, first resolving a cloudId because 3LO tokens are not site-scoped, then requesting only the summary, description, status, labels and reporter fields.

subject: module:agents/jira-reader
claim: Failure modes are mapped to distinct SDK exit codes rather than a generic error: an unparseable issue key yields ExitCode.InvalidInput, a missing JIRA_TOKEN yields ExitCode.MissingCapability, and a failed Jira fetch yields ExitCode.ExternalDependencyFailure.

subject: module:agents/jira-reader
claim: The module owns `numberFromKey`, which derives a GitHub-style issue number from the numeric tail of a Jira key and deliberately returns 0 (not 1) when no positive integer can be derived; this value flows in the issue.summary artifact through planner and coder to pr-opener, where a falsy value suppresses the `Closes #N` line so a merged PR cannot close an unrelated issue.

subject: module:agents/jira-reader
claim: The agent's terminal side effect is a summary artifact: it converts the fetched Jira fields (title, status/state, labels, reporter, plus repository owner/name from the envelope) into an IssueSummary and writes it out, announcing it via an artifact.created event.

subject: module:agents/linear-reader
claim: linear-reader is a single-purpose CLI agent that reads a task envelope from stdin, accepts only the `linear.task.read` task type, and exits with protocol exit codes from @anchorage/sdk (UnsupportedTaskType, InvalidInput, MissingCapability, ExternalDependencyFailure, Success).

subject: module:agents/linear-reader
claim: It fetches an issue from Linear's GraphQL API (default https://api.linear.app/graphql, overridable via LINEAR_API_URL) using a LINEAR_TOKEN OAuth token, querying identifier, title, description, url, state, labels and creator; a missing token is reported as a missing-capability failure rather than attempted.

subject: module:agents/linear-reader
claim: The agent communicates progress by emitting a lifecycle stream of protocol events — agent.started, tool.requested/tool.result, agent.output, artifact.created, agent.completed/agent.failed — and its terminal output is an issue-summary artifact written to disk.

subject: module:agents/linear-reader
claim: It owns the derivation of a GitHub-style issue number from a Linear identifier (`numberFromIdentifier` takes the segment after the last dash), returning 0 rather than a guess when no positive integer exists — a deliberate safety contract because the number flows in the issue.summary artifact to pr-opener's `Closes #N`.

subject: module:agents/linear-reader
claim: Input references are flexible by design: `input.issueRef` may be a human identifier (ENG-123), a raw issue id/UUID, or a Linear issue URL, since Linear's `issue(id:)` resolves both UUID and identifier forms.

subject: module:agents/merge-gate
claim: merge-gate is the terminal agent that actually lands PRs: it consumes a `merge.prepare` task envelope on stdin, rejects any other task type with an UnsupportedTaskType exit, and requires GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_TOKEN to talk to GitHub via Octokit.

subject: module:agents/merge-gate
claim: The module deliberately separates pure merge-decision logic (gate.ts: reviewAllowsMerge, classifyCiStatus, resolveMergeMethod) from the Octokit/network calls in index.ts, so the rules can be unit-tested without a network or a PR.

subject: module:agents/merge-gate
claim: Both gate rules fail closed: only the exact string "approve" from the reviewer permits a merge (so a missing/unreadable review artifact yields "unknown" and refuses), and CI classification treats an unrecognised check conclusion as a failure, with precedence failure > pending > success.

subject: module:agents/merge-gate
claim: A non-approve review is handled as a graceful skip rather than a failure: the agent writes a merge artifact with merged:false, ciStatus "skipped" and a skipReason, emits agent.output/artifact.created/agent.completed events, and exits Success.

subject: module:agents/merge-gate
claim: CI status folds GitHub's two independent surfaces (legacy combined commit statuses and check runs) using shared @anchorage/sdk predicates so merge-gate and ci-watcher share one conclusion vocabulary; the one permissive case is that a repo with no CI configured at all classifies as success.

subject: module:agents/planner
claim: The planner is a standalone CLI agent that reads a TaskEnvelope from stdin, accepts only the `plan.create` task type (exiting with ExitCode.UnsupportedTaskType otherwise), and communicates by emitting protocol events (agent.started, agent.progress, agent.output, artifact.created, agent.completed/failed) with numeric exit codes from @anchorage/sdk.

subject: module:agents/planner
claim: The main pipeline is: resolve an issue summary from the envelope, generate an ImplementationPlan via an LLM tool loop, emit a context snapshot and the plan, persist the plan as an artifact, then optionally post it as a GitHub issue comment.

subject: module:agents/planner
claim: Plan generation depends on the shared @anchorage/agent-llm package for provider resolution, role defaults, prompt blocks, and a tool-calling runtime (repo read, discovery, and web tools), rather than talking to an LLM API directly.

subject: module:agents/planner
claim: GitHub comment rendering and the gating decision are factored into a separately testable `comment.ts` module: `buildPlanComment` renders a deterministic markdown plan (omitting the Risks section when empty) and `shouldPostPlanComment` requires the `github.write` capability, a token, a repository, and a positive integer issue number — deliberately refusing issueNumber 0, the protocol's 'no issue yet' value used by the plan-only flow.

subject: module:agents/planner
claim: Posting the plan comment is explicitly non-fatal: Octokit failures are caught and reported as a tool.result error event without failing the run, so the plan artifact and completion still stand.

subject: module:agents/pr-opener
claim: agents/pr-opener is a standalone CLI agent that reads a TaskEnvelope from stdin, only accepts task type `pull_request.open` (exiting with ExitCode.UnsupportedTaskType otherwise), and communicates progress by emitting protocol events like agent.started/agent.output/artifact.created/agent.completed.

subject: module:agents/pr-opener
claim: It requires a GitHub token from GH_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN and fails fast with ExitCode.MissingCapability when absent, otherwise driving GitHub through an @octokit/rest client.

subject: module:agents/pr-opener
claim: The agent handles the no-op case explicitly: when the upstream code-change result was not pushed and produced no commit, it looks up an already-open PR for the branch and reuses it (emitting warn-level events and still writing the result artifact) instead of publishing a new branch.

subject: module:agents/pr-opener
claim: src/content.ts owns PR text generation as a separately testable unit: it parses the model's JSON reply via the shared `parseModelJsonObject` from @anchorage/sdk, treats only `title` and `why` as required (returning null to route callers to a mechanical fallback), and renders a fixed markdown body of Summary/Why/What/How sections where every section has a non-empty fallback.

subject: module:agents/pr-opener
claim: The module's tests are dependency-free node:test files that exercise the built `dist/content.js` rather than source, pinning parser robustness (never throwing on malformed model output, tolerating code fences and <thinking> blocks containing braces) and the invariant that no PR heading is followed by whitespace.

subject: module:agents/pr-opener
claim: PR content is produced by an LLM call configured through the shared @anchorage/agent-llm package (role defaults, config resolution, completion request), making pr-opener a consumer of the repo's common LLM abstraction rather than talking to a provider directly.

subject: module:agents/reviewer
claim: The reviewer is a standalone CLI agent that reads a task envelope from stdin, accepts only `review.run` tasks, and exits with SDK-defined exit codes (e.g. UnsupportedTaskType, MissingCapability, ExternalDependencyFailure) while emitting protocol events like `agent.started`, `tool.requested`, and `tool.result`.

subject: module:agents/reviewer
claim: It fetches PR review material from GitHub via Octokit — the raw diff (mediaType diff), PR title/body metadata, and the changed file list (listFiles, per_page 100) — requiring a GH_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN and failing with `missing_github_token` / `github_diff_fetch_failed` when unavailable.

subject: module:agents/reviewer
claim: It depends on two shared workspace packages rather than owning that infrastructure: `@anchorage/agent-llm` supplies LLM config resolution, providers, and the tool-running loop plus repo/discovery/web tool sets, while `@anchorage/sdk` supplies envelope validation, exit codes, protocol event types, and revision-request artifact construction.

subject: module:agents/reviewer
claim: `parse.ts` owns the reviewer's model-output recovery layer: it delegates the balanced-brace scan to the shared `extractJsonObject` from `@anchorage/sdk` (deduplicated because three agents had diverging copies) and keeps only this agent's distinct failure vocabulary — missing object vs. non-object vs. invalid JSON — returned as a result type instead of thrown.

subject: module:agents/reviewer
claim: Parsing behaviour is pinned by a dependency-free node:test suite that runs against the built `dist/` output and asserts the recovery paths (code fences, <thinking> blocks, surrounding prose, braces inside strings), the distinguishability of failure messages, and that parsing never throws on malformed input.

subject: module:agents/smoke-test-runner
claim: smoke-test-runner is a stdin-driven CLI agent: it reads a JSON task envelope from fd 0, validates it with @anchorage/sdk's validateTaskEnvelope, rejects any task whose type is not `smoke_test.run`, and returns SDK ExitCode values (InvalidInput, UnsupportedTaskType, PartialSuccessAttentionRequired, Success) as the process result.

subject: module:agents/smoke-test-runner
claim: It executes two kinds of checks — HTTP fetches and shell commands — driven off `input.checks`, with shell checks run relative to an optional `input.workspacePath`, and aggregates every result into a SmokeTestReport whose `passed` is the AND of all check results.

subject: module:agents/smoke-test-runner
claim: The agent communicates progress by emitting a fixed protocol event stream — agent.started, tool.requested/tool.result per check, agent.output, artifact.created, and finally agent.failed or agent.completed — and persists the report as an artifact before exiting.

subject: module:agents/smoke-test-runner
claim: checks.ts owns the check-list parsing abstraction (HttpCheckSpec / ShellCheckSpec / SkippedCheck) and implements a deliberate loud-degrade policy: malformed entries are kept out of the run but returned in a `skipped` list with array index and reason, so a mostly-invalid list cannot silently report `passed`.

subject: module:agents/smoke-test-runner
claim: Parsing applies defensive normalization for untrusted input: expectedStatus defaults to 200 when absent or non-finite, non-string shell args are filtered out before reaching a shell, and unnamed checks receive positional names (`check_N`) — all pinned by a dependency-free node:test suite run against the built dist.

subject: module:agents/tester
claim: The tester agent is a stdin-driven CLI that reads a task envelope from fd 0, accepts only tasks of type `test.run` (emitting `agent.failed` with code `unsupported_task_type` and an UnsupportedTaskType exit otherwise), and emits protocol events such as `agent.started`/`agent.output` via the shared `@anchorage/sdk` contract.

subject: module:agents/tester
claim: Its core owned abstraction is `classifyEnvironment`, which decides whether a non-zero command exit is a genuine test failure or an environment block: exit 0 is never blocked, exit 127 is always blocked, and otherwise stdout+stderr are matched in order against `ENVIRONMENT_FAILURE_PATTERNS` (Docker, Make, Gradle, generic not-found, unreachable services, Go/Node/JDK version skew).

subject: module:agents/tester
claim: Test command resolution follows an explicit fallback chain: `input.commands` (or `input.checks`) wins; if absent, commands are detected from project manifests and then scoped to the projects touched by the coder's changed files; if nothing is detected the run is reported as `skipped: true`, with passing controlled by the `ANCHORAGE_TESTER_REQUIRE_TESTS` strict-mode env var.

subject: module:agents/tester
claim: The classification rules are pinned by a dependency-free node:test suite that runs against the compiled `dist/classify.js`, asserting both the important negative (plain assertion failures stay unblocked) and the deliberate pattern ordering where Docker-specific matches precede the generic 'not found' pattern.

subject: module:agents/tester
claim: The tester participates in a multi-agent loop: it consumes the coder's `code.change.result` changed-file list to scope its runs and can produce a revision request artifact via the SDK's `buildRevisionRequest`/`REVISION_REQUEST_ARTIFACT_TYPE` to feed failures back to the coder.

subject: module:cli/anchorage
claim: cli/anchorage is a dependency-free Node CLI (`anchorage`) that acts as a thin REST shim over the orchestrator API: it hand-rolls its own argv parser rather than using a CLI library, and defines local structural types for API payloads instead of depending on an SDK.

subject: module:cli/anchorage
claim: config.ts owns credential/server resolution with a fixed precedence chain (--server flag > ANCHORAGE_ORCHESTRATOR_URL > ORCHESTRATOR_URL > ~/.config/anchoragelabs/cli.json > https://api.anchoragelabs.dev), deliberately never accepting the secret as a flag, and persists the config file with mode 0600 because it may hold a bearer secret.

subject: module:cli/anchorage
claim: OrchestratorClient is the module's single HTTP boundary to the orchestrator: it prefixes every path with the configured serverUrl, sends the secret twice on each request (Authorization: Bearer and X-Orchestrator-Secret, since the server accepts either), and converts fetch failures and non-2xx JSON error bodies into human-readable Error messages.

subject: module:cli/anchorage
claim: The CLI supports per-agent LLM model overrides: `--agent-model` is registered as a repeatable flag collected into a separate `multi` map, and parseAgentModels turns `<agent>=<provider>:<model>` (or `<agent>=<model>` to keep the global provider) into the agentModels record carried in the run TriggerParams.

subject: module:cli/anchorage
claim: The CLI's surface spans the orchestrator's run lifecycle and account management — auth login/whoami/token rotation, listing and starting runs (by issue or free-form instruction), plus approval gates, diffs and connectors — and models runs from multiple issue sources (GitHub, Notion, Jira, Linear, GitLab, Bitbucket) via TriggerParams.

subject: module:cli/anchorage-runner
claim: cli/anchorage-runner is the executable CLI entrypoint (`anchorage-runner run <agent> < task.json`) that reads a task envelope from stdin, resolves an agent manifest from a name or path, checks agent/task compatibility, and then spawns the agent.

subject: module:cli/anchorage-runner
claim: The runner owns no protocol definitions itself: task envelope, agent manifest, event-stream validation, NDJSON parsing, run-manifest building and exit codes are all imported from the shared `@anchorage/sdk` package, making this module a thin orchestration shell over the SDK.

subject: module:cli/anchorage-runner
claim: Failures are surfaced as distinct SDK exit codes rather than exceptions — invalid JSON, invalid envelope, unsupported protocol major version and invalid manifests map to ExitCode.InvalidInput, a missing agent manifest maps to ExitCode.UnsupportedTaskType — via an internal `RunnerFailure` result type returned from each stage.

subject: module:cli/anchorage-runner
claim: The CLI deliberately splits usage output by intent: `--help`/`-h`/`help` prints to stdout and exits 0, while a wrong invocation prints the same usage to stderr and exits non-zero (ExitCode.InvalidInput); this contract is asserted by spawning the built binary in test/help.test.mjs.

subject: module:cli/anchorage-runner
claim: Only the protocol major version is enforced for compatibility — the runner accepts any `0.x` envelope and rejects other majors, indicating a 0.x-era pinned protocol contract.

subject: module:agents/notion-reader
claim: notion-reader is a standalone CLI agent that reads a task envelope from stdin, validates it with the shared @anchorage/sdk contract, and rejects any task whose type is not `notion.task.read` with the UnsupportedTaskType exit code.

subject: module:agents/notion-reader
claim: The agent communicates progress through a protocol event stream, emitting a fixed lifecycle of `agent.started`, `tool.requested`/`tool.result`, `agent.output`, `artifact.created`, `agent.completed`, and `agent.failed` events, each carrying a structured payload.

subject: module:agents/notion-reader
claim: It integrates with the Notion HTTP API directly (configurable base URL and API version via NOTION_API_BASE_URL/NOTION_VERSION), retrieving a page via `/v1/pages/{id}` plus its body, rather than using an official SDK client.

subject: module:agents/notion-reader
claim: Failures are mapped to distinct SDK exit codes by category: malformed input JSON or an unresolvable page id yields InvalidInput, a missing NOTION_TOKEN/NOTION_API_KEY yields MissingCapability, and a failed Notion fetch yields ExternalDependencyFailure.

subject: module:agents/notion-reader
claim: The agent accepts either a raw page id (dashed or undashed 32-hex) or a Notion page URL via `input.pageId`/`input.pageUrl`, and its successful output is an issue summary artifact keyed by pageId, issueNumber, and title.

subject: module:agents/notion-worker
claim: agents/notion-worker is a standalone CLI agent that reads a task envelope from stdin (fd 0), validates it with @anchorage/sdk's validateTaskEnvelope, and rejects any task whose type is not 'notion.task.act' with ExitCode.UnsupportedTaskType.

subject: module:agents/notion-worker
claim: It communicates progress via a structured protocol event stream, emitting a fixed lifecycle of events — agent.started, tool.requested, tool.result, agent.output, artifact.created, agent.completed — with a monotonic sequence counter and agent version metadata.

subject: module:agents/notion-worker
claim: The agent delegates the actual work to an LLM tool-calling loop from @anchorage/agent-llm (runWithTools with notionReadTools/notionWriteTools and a resolved LlmConfig), rather than calling the Notion API directly itself.

subject: module:agents/notion-worker
claim: Credentials are supplied via environment: the agent requires NOTION_TOKEN or NOTION_API_KEY and fails fast with ExitCode.MissingCapability and a 'missing_notion_token' error code when neither is set.

subject: module:agents/notion-worker
claim: Its output contract is a NotionTaskResult (pageId, pageUrl, summary, operations, risks, model, updatedAt) that is both emitted as agent.output and persisted as an artifact via writeResultArtifact.

subject: module:agents/notion-writer
claim: notion-writer is a standalone CLI agent executable that reads a JSON TaskEnvelope from stdin (fd 0), validates it, and returns an SDK ExitCode as its process result.

subject: module:agents/notion-writer
claim: It handles exactly one task type, `notion.task.update`, rejecting anything else with an `unsupported_task_type` error and ExitCode.UnsupportedTaskType.

subject: module:agents/notion-writer
claim: The agent conforms to a shared host protocol from @anchorage/sdk, emitting a lifecycle event stream (agent.started, tool.requested, tool.result, agent.output, artifact.created, agent.completed/agent.failed) with a monotonically increasing sequence counter.

subject: module:agents/notion-writer
claim: Its concrete side effect is calling the Notion REST API: it posts a workflow summary comment to POST /v1/comments for a page id and optionally updates the page status, authenticating with NOTION_TOKEN or NOTION_API_KEY and failing with ExitCode.MissingCapability when neither is set.

subject: module:agents/notion-writer
claim: Notion connection details are environment-configurable (NOTION_API_BASE_URL, NOTION_VERSION defaulting to api.notion.com and API version 2022-06-28), and outbound text is split to respect Notion's 2000-character rich_text limit.

subject: module:agents/notion-writer
claim: On success the agent produces a persisted artifact describing the update (pageId, pageUrl, commentPosted, status, updatedAt) that downstream consumers can pick up via the artifact.created event.

subject: module:agents/policy-check
claim: policy-check is a standalone CLI agent that reads a TaskEnvelope from stdin, accepts only tasks of type `policy.check`, and emits protocol events (agent.started/output/completed/failed) with SDK exit codes for unsupported task types and invalid input.

subject: module:agents/policy-check
claim: The module owns no policy engine of its own: it delegates constraint parsing and rule evaluation to `@anchorage/agent-llm` (`parseConstraints`, `evaluateForbidImports`, `getIndexStore`) and protocol/envelope concerns to `@anchorage/sdk` (`validateTaskEnvelope`, `buildRevisionRequest`, `ExitCode`), acting as the orchestration glue between them.

subject: module:agents/policy-check
claim: Governance is opt-in and fails open: a missing or unreadable `.anchorage/constraints.yaml` in the workspace, or a file with zero enforceable graph rules, completes successfully rather than erroring, distinguished in the event payload by `checked: false` vs `checked: true, ruleCount: 0`.

subject: module:agents/policy-check
claim: Rules are evaluated only against files changed relative to the repository's default branch, using an import-graph view built from a persisted symbol index; when that index is unavailable the agent still proceeds but emits a `graphAvailable: false` warning so an unenforceable run is not mistaken for a genuine all-clear.

subject: module:agents/policy-check
claim: Violations are partitioned by severity into hard and soft buckets, and the agent can produce a revision-request artifact via the SDK's `buildRevisionRequest` / `REVISION_REQUEST_ARTIFACT_TYPE`, indicating it feeds corrective work back into the agent pipeline rather than only reporting.

subject: module:protocol
claim: The protocol module defines the system's wire contracts as JSON Schema 2020-12 documents under protocol/schemas — namely artifact-reference, agent-manifest, protocol-event, and task-envelope — published under the https://anchorage.dev/schemas/ $id namespace.

subject: module:protocol
claim: Conformance is enforced by a fixture-driven harness: validate-test-cases.mjs compiles all schemas with Ajv 2020 in strict mode (plus ajv-formats) and asserts that every JSON file in test-cases/valid/* validates and every file in test-cases/invalid/* fails, exiting non-zero on any mismatch.

subject: module:protocol
claim: The three externally exercised protocol surfaces are tasks, events, and manifests: only task-envelope, protocol-event, and agent-manifest have valid/invalid fixture directories, while artifact-reference is loaded only as a supporting schema for $ref resolution.

subject: module:protocol
claim: The harness is self-contained and path-relative (resolving schemas/ and test-cases/ from the script's own location via import.meta.url) with no imports from other repository modules, so the protocol module is a standalone contract package rather than runtime library code.
